questions.prompt: Why does the eval prompt say 'check this FASTA file' and not 'use the check-fasta skill'?
questions.explain: Real users do not name the Skill. If the test names it, it cannot tell you whether the description triggers it.

options.text: It checks the description fires on a natural request
Naming a Skill in a prompt is not allowed by the tool at all
options.misconception: You can name a Skill. The point is that users usually will not.

options.text: It makes the run cheaper by shortening the prompt text
options.misconception: Prompt length is not the reason. Cost comes from the number of runs and judge calls.

questions.prompt: Which grader types cost no model calls?
questions.explain: regex, tool_used, tool_order and file_exists are computed from the transcript or files. llm and baseline use a judge model.

options.misconception: These two ask a judge model, which is a paid call.

options.text: All of them, since the agent is already running
options.misconception: Judge-model graders add extra paid calls on top of the run.

questions.prompt: In a with/without run the difference is near zero and the Skill never fires. What is the most likely cause?
questions.explain: A Skill that never fires cannot change anything. The description probably does not match how the request was phrased.

options.text: The description does not trigger on that phrasing
The grader is too strict and needs loosening
options.misconception: A strict grader would lower both arms. A zero difference with no firing points at the trigger.
They can, and this pattern is one of the things they are good at showing.

questions.prompt: Which line makes this cheap first run costly?
questions.explain: Raising runs and cases multiplies paid calls. For first iterations use one case, one run and no baseline arm.

lines.why: One case, one run, no baseline arm: the cheap form.
A cost ceiling makes spending predictable.

questions.prompt: Your eval case passes. What have you learned?
questions.explain: The case passed in an isolated session with only this plugin. It says little about your own setup and nothing about whether the plugin is safe.

options.text: It behaved on that case, in isolation
The plugin is safe to share with the whole group
options.misconception: Evals measure behaviour on cases, not safety. Hooks or scripts could still do harm.

options.text: The Skill will behave the same in every project you open
options.misconception: The run had no personal settings, instructions file or other plugins, so your own setup may differ.

questions.prompt: An agent finishes a task and writes 'all checks passed'. What is the stronger way to confirm it?
questions.explain: An agent marking its own work is not independent. A script, a separate verifier or a person should check the changed files and cite evidence.

options.text: A separate verifier or script checks the files and cites evidence
Ask the same agent to read its answer again and confirm it
options.misconception: The same agent can repeat its own mistake, so this is not an independent check.

options.text: Trust the claim, because the Skill told the agent to verify its work
options.misconception: Instructions guide the agent but prove nothing. Tests and review do the verifying.
